title: the-loop gateway configuration (gateway-config.yaml)
description: The gateway's own file (issue-496): one process that owns every inbound transport (GitHub and Jira webhooks, Slack Socket Mode and HTTP routes, the pollers), stores each event on a per-work-item subject before acknowledging the provider, and fans it out on write to the queue of every instance that consumes that subject. Instances poll their queue over `cli-config.yaml`'s `gateway` block. Separate from `cli-config.yaml` on purpose: a gateway on another box carries none of an instance's keys. Every secret is NAMED here (a `*Env` key) and read from the process environment; `env.file` names the dotenv file that holds the values. Validated by `the-loop gateway start`, which refuses to start on a violation naming the path; hot-reloaded on the five-second hash cadence, except `listen` and the Slack tokens, which need `the-loop gateway restart`.

env.description: A dotenv file the gateway loads first, before any ingress reads the environment — the same rule as `cli-config.yaml`'s `env` block (issue-318): a relative path resolves against THIS file's directory, `~` expands, a variable already set is never overwritten, a missing or malformed file is a warning naming the path and never a value. Not re-read on reload.

file.description: Path of the dotenv file (one NAME=value per line). Unset or empty: nothing is loaded.

state.description: Where the gateway's generated state lives: its pidfile, logfile, event log and store. Separate from any instance's `state.root` so a gateway and an instance can share one machine (R14).

root.description: The state root. A relative value resolves against this file's directory; `~` expands.

listen.description: The address the gateway binds. Loopback by default; a non-loopback bind without `exposed: true` refuses to start (the service's own rule, decision-059). The instance-to-gateway boundary carries no authentication in this release: an exposed gateway is readable, claimable and committable by any peer on that network.

port.description: Bind port. Differs from the service (4114) and the stdlib receiver (8787) so all three start on one laptop with no configuration.

exposed.description: Acknowledge that a non-loopback bind is reachable without authentication. Required for any host outside 127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1.

store.description: The queue store: SQLite from the standard library, in the state root. No broker is required to run a gateway (R6.5).

path.description: The database file. Unset resolves to `<state.root>/gateway.db`.

retentionDays.description: Committed deliveries older than this are deleted; pending deliveries and events held on `unassigned` older than this are expired and recorded as `subject.expired`; dead-lettered rows are kept for twice this.

maxAttempts.description: Fetches of one delivery before it is dead-lettered and committed (`subject.dead-lettered`). `polling.maxRetries`' sibling.

dedupWindow.description: How many dedup keys the store keeps beyond retention, so a provider's late redelivery of an expired event is still recognised.

consume.description: Bounds on the consumer API (`POST /api/v1/gateway/fetch`): what an instance may ask for, clamped server-side.

maxBatch.description: The most deliveries one fetch returns; a larger `max` is clamped.

maxWaitSeconds.description: The longest a long-poll is held open; a larger `wait` is clamped. 0 disables long-polling for every instance.

leaseSeconds.description: The window within which a second peer fetching under a live instance name is refused with 409 `duplicate-instance` (R4.3). The client asks for `3 × pollIntervalSeconds + longPollSeconds`; the gateway clamps it into this range.

repositories.description: GitHub repositories (`owner/repo`) whose issues and pull requests may be work items. An event on a repository not listed here is dropped (`gateway.dropped: undeclared-repository`).

github.description: GitHub's two transports, enableable independently. The poller is the default (no public URL needed) and the reconciliation path when both run (R7.4); the same comment arriving by both stores one row (R7.3).

webhook.description: `POST /gh-webhook` under GitHub's own contract: the `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC the instance's receiver verifies today, so a webhook re-pointed at the gateway needs no change.

secretEnv.description: The webhook secret. The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

poll.description: Poll the declared repositories through the GitHub API, producing the same delivery ids the instance poller produces (`poll-comment-<id>`, …).

enabled.description: Run the gateway's own GitHub poller. Opt-in (off by default): the instances keep their own pollers behind a gateway, and the gateway is the webhook receiver and the Slack connection unless no inbound webhook is possible, in which case turn this on and the gateway polls for the fleet.

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between polls of each source.

tokenEnv.description: A token with READ access to the declared repositories. The gateway never posts; posting stays on the instance. The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

sources.description: One entry per repository to poll. Each must also be in `repositories`.

labels.description: Only items carrying every one of these labels are listed (the instance's `routing.autoExecuteLabels` is the usual set). Empty: every open item.

jira.description: Jira's two transports. Off by default; poll-only in the first proof (R12.6).

webhook.description: `POST /jira-webhook` under the instance doorbell's secret contract; 404 with no secret configured, as today.

secretEnv.description: The webhook secret. The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

poll.description: Poll the mapped projects through the Jira API.

enabled.description: Run the gateway's own Jira poller. Opt-in (off by default), as for GitHub.

site.description: The Jira site (`your-org.atlassian.net`) the poller and the key-to-ref mapping use.

emailEnv.description: The account email for basic auth (Cloud). The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

tokenEnv.description: The API token. The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

labels.description: Only issues carrying every one of these labels are listed.

projects.description: Project keys whose issues may be work items. An event on a project not listed here is dropped (`gateway.dropped: unbound`).

slack.description: Slack's two transports for one app. Socket Mode is the default (no public URL) and exactly one connection is opened per app for the life of the process (R1.2); the HTTP routes verify Slack's `v0` signature within the 300 s replay window.

appTokenEnv.description: The app-level token (`connections:write`). The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

botTokenEnv.description: The bot token, for the heartbeat split check and for posting on the instances' behalf (issue-519, `slack.post`). The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

splitCheckBeats.description: Heartbeats to miss before `channel.split_suspected`, as the instance's `channels.slack.read.splitCheckBeats`.

signingSecretEnv.description: The app's signing secret. The NAME of an environment variable, never a value: a pasted token fails validation here (issue-496, abuse case 7).

post.description: Outbound Slack for the instances (issue-519): the gateway makes the Slack Web API calls an instance asks for — posts, edits, reactions, thread reads, file downloads — with the bot token its Socket Mode ingress already holds, so an instance behind a gateway needs no Slack token of its own. A pass-through: nothing is stored or retried here, and a call the gateway cannot make fails the instance's post.

enabled.description: Make Slack Web API calls for the instances (issue-519). On by default: the token is already here. `false` answers every call with `503 posting-unavailable`, and an instance without a bot token of its own then says at start and in `status` that it cannot post. Hot-reloaded; no restart.

rooms.description: Channel-to-work-item declarations: a thread in a declared channel that no binding covers resolves to this work item. A thread outside any room and any binding is dropped (`gateway.dropped: unbound`).

instances.description: Optional allow-list of instance names. When set, a fetch, claim or registration under another name is refused (`gateway.refused: unknown-instance`). A guard against misconfiguration, not an authentication.

observability.description: The gateway's event log: the same JSONL shape as every the-loop process (decision-025), under the `gateway.*` and `subject.*` families.
